question.text: Vindhya Event-Driven Fund holds pre-IPO shares of 'Surya Foods Pvt Ltd' which is now launching its IPO. The issue is NOT predominantly for capital expenditure (i.e. ordinary IPO). Under SEBI (ICDR) Regulations 2018, what lock-in applies to the fund's pre-issue holding (other than minimum promoter contribution)?

answer.text: 6 months from date of allotment in the public issue
No lock-in applies to Cat III AIFs

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI (ICDR) Regulations 2018, the entire pre-issue share capital of an unlisted company (other than minimum promoter contribution) is locked in for 6 MONTHS from date of allotment in the public issue. Where majority of fresh-issue proceeds is for CapEx, the lock-in is 1 year. A Cat II or Cat III AIF is subject to this lock-in. The Trap: Option A (18 months) is the minimum-promoter-contribution lock-in for ordinary IPOs. Option B (3 years) applies to promoter contribution for CapEx-dominant IPOs. Option D is wrong. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D, XIX-C test ICDR lock-ins. XIX-E cares for event-driven Cat III pre-IPO exits. Manager's Pro-Tip: For event-driven or activist Cat III strategies, model lock-ins into your exit plan. OFS route via T-1 notice is available only after lock-in — no shortcut.
